description: D15 pre-registration for the 2026-08-21 44.5s source-detail page incident. Two independently shippable fixes: (1) idx_pg_records_instance_stream_id, closing the missing keyset index that made BOTH the page query and the semantic backfill's own coverage scan multi-second; (2) a separate bulk connection lane with a Postgres-enforced statement/lock ceiling, closing the pool-starvation half. Every bound below was measured live on 2026-08-21 BEFORE any deploy.

artifactAssertions.description: The keyset-index migration must be present in the built image. Measured 2026-08-21: this symbol is absent from the running pdpp-core:drain33 and present in the branch source, so this grep alone distinguishes 'deployed' from 'restarted onto the same bytes'.
The bulk connection lane must be present in the built image. Same deployed-vs-restarted discrimination as above, for the second of the two fixes.

checks.description: PRIMARY METRIC. idx_pg_records_instance_stream_id must exist AND be both valid and ready. Measured live 2026-08-21 BEFORE deploy: 0 (the index does not exist; the page query plans Index Scan using records_pkey, 27.4s, Rows Removed by Filter 3,031,420). Expected after deploy: 1. indisvalid/indisready are the load-bearing part, not mere existence: an interrupted CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY leaves the index present but INVALID, the planner ignores it, and the slow plan silently returns -- so a bare existence check would report success on exactly the failure mode this build's CONCURRENTLY path can produce.
checks.sql: select count(*) from pg_index ix join pg_class c on c.oid=ix.indexrelid join pg_namespace n on n.oid=c.relnamespace where n.nspname='public' and c.relname='idx_pg_records_instance_stream_id' and ix.indisvalid and ix.indisready

checks.description: No client statement may run past the 15s bulk ceiling. Measured live 2026-08-21: 0 at sample time -- but this is a POINT-IN-TIME sample and 0 here is partly luck, so it is meaningful only as a guard against regression, not as evidence the defect was absent. During the incident this same query returned non-zero repeatedly (records-page statements sampled at 22.3s and 27.4s). Excludes autovacuum, which is a maintenance backend and legitimately long-running.
checks.sql: select count(*) from pg_stat_activity where datname='pdpp' and state='active' and backend_type='client backend' and query not like '%pg_stat_activity%' and now()-query_start > interval '15 seconds'

checks.description: The specific statement shape from the incident -- the keyset page over `records` that both the source-detail page and the semantic backfill issue -- must not be observed running past 5s. Measured live 2026-08-21: successive backfill pages sampled at 1.2s, 1.6s, 1.9s, 7.0s, 12.2s, 17.2s, 22.3s and 27.4s, so a 5s bound is comfortably above the healthy cost and well below the observed pathology. Post-index this shape measured 1.4-1.7ms at production-representative volume regardless of cursor depth.
checks.sql: select count(*) from pg_stat_activity where datname='pdpp' and state='active' and backend_type='client backend' and query like '%FROM records%' and query like '%ORDER BY id ASC%' and now()-query_start > interval '5 seconds'

checks.description: BEHAVIOR PRESERVATION (D14). Neither fix may add, drop or soft-delete a record: an index changes access paths only, and routing bulk work to a second pool changes which connection runs a statement, not what it writes. Measured live 2026-08-21 by executing this exact SQL: 5,614,451 live rows. must_not_decrease rather than must_equal because ordinary ingest legitimately adds rows during the canary window.
checks.sql: select count(*) from records where deleted = false

checks.description: BEHAVIOR PRESERVATION (D14) for the bulk WRITE path specifically. postgresSemanticIndexInsertManyGuarded moved onto the bulk lane; its single-statement version-CAS is unchanged, so its output must be too. A drop here would mean the bulk statement_timeout is cancelling real backfill work rather than acting as a backstop -- the most plausible way this change could do harm. Measured live 2026-08-21 by executing this exact SQL immediately before deploy: 65,146.

RestartCount must not climb. Measured live 2026-08-21: 0 on pdpp-core-prod-drain. A climbing count means the supervisor is crash-looping behind a container that still reports 'Up' -- the relevant risk here being a boot-time migration that wedges.
The running image tag must differ from the pre-image: the artifact greps prove the bytes are right, this proves the container actually picked them up.
uncaughtException must not appear in the post-deploy window.

The bulk statement_timeout is a BACKSTOP, not a routine cliff. Measured bulk writes on this instance run 0.5-1.1s against a 15s ceiling, so it should never fire in normal operation; if it does, the ceiling is mis-sized or something regressed, and either way the operator should see it rather than have backfill silently shedding chunks. Non-blocking: a single fire is a signal to investigate, not a reason to roll back a deploy that is otherwise healthy.
The reference server must answer. /owner/login returns 200 unauthenticated and is server-rendered, so a 200 proves the app is serving rather than that a port is open.
